highlights.title: Man unexpectedly recovers from a knife wound through his eye and brain
highlights.summary: A man in his 20s showed up to a UK hospital with the hilt of a knife sticking out of his face. The 15 mm blade hidden within went completely through his right eye and through his brain, with the tip of the blade hitting the top of his skull.
body: Despite the ghastly injury, the man was alive and conscious when he arrived. He could still talk and move all four limbs. His doctors described him as being in a state of agitation. On the Glasgow Coma Scale, he scored a 12 (E3 V4 M5), indicating a "moderate" brain injury, just one point above "mild." He could open his left eye when told, but otherwise kept it closed (E3 score); he could talk and answer questions, but was confused (V4); and he intentionally moved away when pressure was applied to his body (M5).

In a report published Friday in BMJ Case Report, his doctors said they were concerned that in his confused, agitated state he may try to pull the knife out on his own. So, they swiftly sedated and intubated him. They put him on prophylactic treatments for bacterial infections, including tetanus. Then they used images to see what was going on in his head.

The 15 mm blade hidden within went completely through his right eye and through his brain, with the tip of the blade hitting the top of his skull.

highlights.title: OpenAI valued at $1.25 trillion, as rival Anthropic nears its IPO
highlights.summary: OpenAI is now valued at $1.25 trillion in a new round of funding that has raised another $11 billion, according to Bloomberg. That would make it one of the world's most valuable companies, not long after raising $122 billion from investors in March at a valuation of $852 billion.
body: CEO Sam Altman said recently that OpenAI is prioritizing safety instead of going ‘guns blazing’ toward an IPO.

Echoing FT and Wall Street Journal reports from last week, Bloomberg says OpenAI is still pursuing additional investments that could increase the amount to $20 billion, and that it had initially hoped to raise as much as $30 billion at a higher valuation of $1.4 trillion. That was before tech stocks dropped, and the results of the midterms showed how much public opinion has turned against AI companies and data center projects.

OpenAI’s rival Anthropic filed its S-1 to go public last week. Earlier this year, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said it’s holding off on its own IPO until it can make more confident claims about its models’ safety. He didn’t give a specific timeline for the IPO, but said at the time, “I think it’s also kind of bad for the world if OpenAI waits too long to go public.”

highlights.title: EA HQ Graced With 'Save Mass Effect' Truck as N7 Day Looms
highlights.summary: Mass Effect fans have taken their mission to save BioWare and its beloved sci-fi franchise to EA headquarters with a truck displaying the #SaveMassEffect message.
body: The latest update to what has ballooned into a full-blown movement arrived today when the dedicated group of fans known as We are Mass Effect announced they had brought their latest billboard right to the publisher's front door. Where their last push arrived in the form of a daylong billboard in New York City's Times Square, this mobile effort will see a truck sharing the word on the streets surrounding EA and EA Sports HQ in Redwood City, California.

Anyone who visits the area today can spot the truck, which features signage updated with a handy QR code and website URL directing curious players to SaveMassEffect.com. The goal, as We are Mass Effect's Mer told IGN, is to "spread the word and bring as much attention to the movement as possible, " but putting it in EA's front lawn after the publisher put Mass Effect games on hold and shuttered BioWare also sends a message of its own.

highlights.title: Paul Howard, Son of Moe Howard of The Three Stooges, Dies at 91
highlights.summary: Paul Howard, son of The Three Stooges’ Moe Howard, died earlier this week in Manhattan. He was 91. Paul Howard remained a guardian of his father’s legacy throughout his life, meeting generations of Stooges fans at conventions and events where he shared personal stories, family memories and insights…
body: “Dad [Moe] always wanted a son; someone he could take fishing and with whom he could play baseball. In late 1934, after Mother informed him that she was pregnant, he quipped, ‘Honey, if it’s a boy, they’ll have to drag me out of the gutter, I’ll be so drunk.’

Mother timed Paul’s birth to a vaudeville tour in the east so she could give birth to Paul at Doctor’s Hospital in New York. … On July 8, 1935, eight years after I was born, Dad’s dream became a reality when my brother Paul was born.

“Dad, who did not drink, was drunk with glee. Though I know he loved me, he was so proud to have a son. Paul was actually born two blocks away from where he lives today in the Yorkville section of Manhattan.

As the realization of what had transpired hit him, Dad found himself in a more precarious situation: Aunt Clarice’s water suddenly broke.Dad laughed hysterically. “This only happens in a Stooge comedy.”

highlights.title: When the Chanel circus came to Sydney it brought bespoke barricades and 800 VICs
highlights.summary: Celebrities including Nicole Kidman, Margot Robbie and Kylie Minogue sat front row at two runway events while bemused locals looked on. They came, they saw, they CC’d.
body: They came, they saw, they CC’d. This week Chanel – the world’s second-biggest luxury brand after Louis Vuitton, with sales of US$19.3bn in 2025 – mobilised an estimated team of 300 in Sydney, staging a “replica” presentation of its Cruise 2026/2027 collection, first shown in Biarritz in April.

Its celebrity guest list was headlined by Nicole Kidman, Margot Robbie, Kylie Minogue and Baz Lurhmann. Staff included many of its head office team (French accents were omnipresent), a local production company and about 80 models, 50 of them internationally based.
Traditionally, Chanel stages a smaller-scale repeat Cruise show in November each year as the collection hits stores; recent destinations include Singapore, Hong Kong and Miami.

This year, for the first time, Sydney was singled out as worthy of particular attention. Little wonder, given that half of Chanel’s eight freestanding Australian boutiques are located in the harbour city. Last year, the company made just over half a billion dollars in sales revenue in Australia, according to documents lodged with the Australian Securities and Investments Commission.

highlights.title: Starlink Mobile: All the news on SpaceX’s major mobile carrier ambitions
highlights.summary: SpaceX has declared that it’s going to make Starlink Mobile a “major” mobile carrier. The Elon Musk-owned company has already deployed thousands of direct-to-cell satellites, but its next big challenge is building out its 5G network here on Earth.
body: As part of its plans to rival AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile, SpaceX has inked a deal with Qualcomm, which will deploy its cellular technology across tens of thousands of 5G cell sites starting in 2027. SpaceX is also reportedly in talks to buy Boost Mobile, potentially allowing it to launch Starlink Mobile through the service. Another report suggests SpaceX may tap into 80,000 cell sites across the US to build out its network.

SpaceX’s big plans have garnered some reactions in the telecom industry. Tim Höttges, the CEO of T-Mobile’s parent company Deutsche Telekom, said he takes SpaceX’s plans “super serious” but that it could cost Musk more than $200 billion to pull off.
Follow along for the latest updates on Starlink’s major mobile carrier ambitions.
Today, I’m talking with Walter Piecyk, a partner and analyst at LightShed Partners who covers tech, media, and telecom, about SpaceX’s recently announced plan to become a major wireless carrier.

body: The former Australia batter said the team used sandpaper to tamper with the ball before Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera while handling the object during the third Test, ahead of the release of Khawaja’s autobiography Sabr on Tuesday.

Bancroft, David Warner and Steve Smith were the only players sanctioned after a Cricket Australia investigation found the trio had prior knowledge of the scheme to use sandpaper as a ball tampering agent in Cape Town.
Captain Smith and Vice-captain Warner were suspended for 12 months for their parts in the plot, while Bancroft was handed a nine-month ban for using sandpaper on the ball.
“It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us,” Khawaja says in his book, according to Nine newspapers.

highlights.title: Avery the Poké Kid's Father Pleads With The Pokémon Company to Make a Trading Card in Honor of His Late Son
highlights.summary: The father of late Pokémon influencer Avery the Poké Kid is asking The Pokémon Company to create a special card in honor of his son. Avery the Poké Kid was a prominent and cheerful voice in the Pokémon Trading Card Game community.
body: Now, his father is putting forth a public request to The Pokémon Company to make a special card in Avery’s honor.
On November 6, Christian Garcia — Avery’s father — published a tearful video on Instagram with a special plea to "immortalize" his son in the hobby he loved the most.

“Trying to figure out how to carry on Avery’s legacy has been the biggest challenge of the last couple months,” Garcia said. “…I want to make a plea to anyone, literally anyone from The Pokémon Company: If you’re watching this video, I want to figure out how to immortalize him somehow in the trading card game he loved so much.

“That kid literally was the embodiment of a Pokémon Master, and we’re hopeful, and I think it would be the coolest thing to open up a pack of cards and chase our son. If someone at The Pokémon Company is watching, please get a hold of us.”

highlights.title: ‘Jimmy’ Review: Cornball James Stewart Biopic Gets the Manner, but Not the Man
highlights.summary: As one of Hollywood’s staunchest Republicans, the late James Stewart perhaps wouldn’t be rolling in his grave in response to “Jimmy,” a biopic that — in focusing rather less on his artistry than on his military service — paints him in a glowingly conservative light.
body: KJ Apa does a passable Stewart impression in this one-note, semi-faith-based portrait, which mainly portrays the beloved Hollywood star as a vessel for patriotic values.

Directed by Aaron Burns — whose previous two features were both produced by the streaming arm of Christian studio Affirm Films — and released by Fathom Entertainment, “Jimmy” isn’t explicitly faith-based, but it is at least faith-adjacent, with much emphasis on Stewart’s Presbyterian background, and more than one moment of religious epiphany when the chips are down. Not by accident is its most detailed glimpse of its subject’s Hollywood career a reconstruction of the famous bridge prayer scene in “It’s a Wonderful Life” — the scene that Stewart himself identified as his favorite from all his films.

highlights.title: Ships loiter near subsea cables amid Iran's warnings to Trump
highlights.summary: Several tanker ships linked to Iran have been loitering over subsea Internet cables in the Gulf of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz—a possible indication that the Iranian government is preparing to attack such undersea infrastructure in response to any renewed US and Israeli strikes.
body: The movements of three sanctioned tankers and an Iranian fishing boat have been tracked near major undersea cables by the maritime intelligence firm Windward in October, according to the Financial Times. Six active cables currently cross through the contested Strait of Hormuz, linking the Middle East to Europe, Africa and Asia, with two more cables having segments under construction in the region.

Four countries, including Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar, depend entirely upon such subsea telecommunications connections running through the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint to link with the outside world. But other countries also depend heavily on the region’s undersea cable network—one third of India’s westbound Internet traffic goes through the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz.
One cable under construction, the 2Africa cable, is owned by a tech consortium that includes the US company Meta. That was one of the major cable corridors visited by the drifting Iran-linked ships.

highlights.title: How to predict the behavior of molecules from scant data
highlights.summary: A machine-learning approach called CheMeleon provides a practical way to develop new drugs or other molecules with much less detailed, expensive experimentation.
body: Discovering new molecules for specific uses is a major driver of progress in a wide variety of industries, whether it’s pharmaceutical companies looking for new drugs, or electronics or energy companies seeking new materials with particular properties. But it’s also largely a trial-and-error process, because there is not yet any way to perfectly predict how a given chemical compound will behave in terms of the myriad different properties and responses materials can exhibit.

Recent progress has been made on using artificial intelligence and machine learning to supplement or speed up laborious calculations based on physical principles that can at least provide some initial guidance on which compounds might be worth synthesizing and testing. Now, a new method developed at MIT shows that when there are few data on some technologically relevant property, such as ligand affinities for a recently discovered cellular target for a potential drug, this approach can outperform other existing methods for winnowing down the field of possible molecules that might be worth looking at.

highlights.title: All Happy Mask Shop buyer locations in Zelda Ocarina of Time
highlights.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake's Happy Mask Shop quest sends you around Hyrule peddling masks to specific customers. That sounds like a cushy gig, except you have very little guidance about who your customers are, and you occasionally even have to pay back the cost of the mask, too.
body: Below, we walk you through each step of the Ocarina of Time remake's Happy Mask Shop quest and explain what you get for your trouble.

Visit the Happy Mask Shop in Hyrule Castle Town as Young Link at any point during the adventure after you've met Princess Zelda and given her letter to the Death Mountain gatekeeper. The shop is in Castle Town square, and it's only open during the daytime.

Speak with the salesman to get started. He'll offer you a gig selling masks, and the first one is the Keaton Mask. He tells you the going cost is 10 rupees, which means that's how much you have to pay him after selling the mask, and then sends you off. This pattern repeats for the rest of the quest. After delivering a mask, you must pay the salesman the going cost to get the next one. Your customers won't always pay the going cost, either, so you'll frequently have to foot the bill yourself.

highlights.title: The Cybertruck’s Death Is Actually Great News for EVs
highlights.summary: Tesla’s massive EV is the second within the last year to get the ax, while smaller vehicles are proliferating. It could be a huge benefit for the US battery supply chain.
body: Tesla will end production of the Cybertruck at its Texas Gigafactory next year.
It’s a uniquely toxic electric vehicle, between its divisive design and Elon Musk’s embrace of you name it. That toxicity certainly contributed to subpar sales, along with a number of recalls.

But the end of the Cybertruck is also another sign that the era of big EVs—particularly big trucks—is waning. That’s great news for pedestrian and biker safety, but also for the battery supply chain at a time when more people need to get behind the electric wheel.

The Cybertruck uses a massive 123 kilowatt-hour battery that clocks in at around 1,600 pounds, or around a quarter of its weight. That’s on par with the battery that powered Ford’s F-150 Lightning, another electric truck that was canceled late last year. (The company also killed a three-row EV in 2024.) Ford’s behemoth batteries ranged from 98 kilowatt-hours up to 131 kilowatt-hours.

highlights.summary: Audio recording on practice courts will be deactivated at the WTA Finals after private comments made by Jessica Pegula about Mirra Andreeva were picked up, with the governing body's chair apologising to the American for the "regrettable" incident.
body: US player Pegula describing Russian teenager Andreeva as "a diva" while conversing with coach Mark Knowles during a practice session were heard on a YouTube livestream at Indian Wells, the venue for the WTA Tour season-ending event from November 8-15.

The WTA shouldered the blame for failing to properly inform players about active microphones, with chair Valerie Camillo saying there was "a lack of advanced notice and clear signage" as she confirmed audio will now be switched off for practice sessions.
Camillo added: "I want to specifically apologise to Jessica Pegula and [coach] Mark Knowles. What happened was regrettable and unacceptable.
"Jess is one of the WTA's best advocates and biggest stars. She does not deserve this distraction.

highlights.title: Free Chinese AI Models Are Getting Scary Good at Hacking
highlights.summary: An experiment in which AI models were asked to break into simulated networks showed the hacking skills of DeepSeek and GLM to be not far behind OpenAI’s most advanced cyber model, which isn’t public.
body: Open-weight artificial intelligence models are now almost as capable of hacking into computer networks as the best closed ones, according to new research that heralds a much-anticipated turning point in the cybersecurity landscape.
Vals, a company that measures AI capabilities, set out to test how well different AI models could carry out complex, multi-step network instructions on mock corporate networks.

“The best frontier models, locked up inside the labs and available only through trusted access programs, are now starting to be matched by open models that anybody can download,” says Nikil Ravi, a researcher at Vals.

The company’s findings suggest that closed models no longer have a definitive edge in cyber skills, meaning recent efforts by frontier labs to limit access to their models, and thereby slow the proliferation of such capabilities, may potentially be moot.

highlights.title: ‘Minimal look, maximal politics’: how the black T-shirt became a political weapon
highlights.summary: The look – worn by Abdul El-Sayed, Andy Burnham and Volodymyr Zelenskyy – radiates authority and no-nonsense masculinity, say fashion experts. For years the black T-shirt was consigned to the clothing category of plain basics. A hidden layer rather than the main event.
body: The progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who this week became the first Muslim elected to the US Senate in history, made a tight black T-shirt his signature look throughout his year-long campaign. Styling it with jeans and friendship bracelets made by his children, El-Sayed described his attire as “minimal look, maximal politics”.
In sharp contrast to the Maga aesthetic of boxy suits, El-Sayed’s T-shirt softens the lines between politics and the public. It’s anti-establishment without being alienating.
“Black radiates authority, seriousness, a certain no-nonsense masculinity,” says Johnny Davis, the luxury director of Esquire magazine.
A black T-shirt has also become a key part of Andy Burnham’s “man of the people” look – so much so that Kemi Badenoch once described the prime minister as a “pair of eyelashes and a black T-shirt”.

highlights.title: Lampard: VAR didn't do its job
highlights.summary: Coventry boss Frank Lampard says VAR 'didn't do its job' in his side's defeat to Everton as three reviews controversially went against his side.
body: Two penalty appeals and a possible handball for Everton's second goal were all reviewed by VAR officials Timothy Wood and Gary Beswick, but nothing was given. They were also not awarded on-field by referee Stuart Attwell.
Coventry opened the scoring after the two penalty appeals, but were ultimately beaten 3-1 on Merseyside on Friday Night Football.
Lampard told Sky Sports: "I hate to sound like a moaner. It's a football match and if you win the game, that can happen here. I've worked here and know the momentum swings in the game.
"I'm not trying to talk about the circumstances of the actual football, but when big decisions change games, they absolutely do. It's disappointing. VAR is there for that and it didn't do its job."

highlights.title: Where to get Epona in Ocarina of Time
highlights.summary: Epona is your trusty steed in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. Hyrule Field is a large zone, and running across it can take a long time. So, speed up the process a bit by calling Epona to your side. However, you'll need to wait a bit before you can ride her.
body: After you wake up Malon's Dad, Talon, outside of Hyrule Castle, you can first find Epona at Lon Lon Ranch beside Malon. However, Epona will run away if you get too close. If you talk to Malon, she'll tell you that Epona is a little shy around strangers, but she likes music. Take out your ocarina, and Malon will teach you Epona's Song ( X - Y - A - X - Y - A ). Play it, and Epona will come running over. However, as Epona is just a small horse and Link is but a child, you won't be able to ride Epona right away.

Once you have all the Spiritual Stones and can travel into the future, return to Lon Lon Ranch, which has been taken over by Ingo and is now named Ingo Ranch, during the daytime. You'll find Ingo by the field, and he'll make you pay 20 rupees to ride a horse. Once inside, play Epona's Song, and she'll come running over. Ride her over to Ingo, and he'll challenge you to a race.

highlights.title: Albert Brooks Predicted Ozempic. Now He’s Predicting President Ossoff
highlights.summary: In his 2011 novel 'Twenty Thirty,' he imagined a blockbuster weight-loss drug, a generational war — and a Jewish president. "God damn it," he recently told a friend. "My entire book is going to come true.”
body: By the fifth sentence of Twenty Thirty, Albert Brooks already looks like a modern-day Nostradamus. At an 80th birthday party in the 2011 novel, everyone looks suspiciously good, due in part to “a new weight-loss drug” that “works almost 100 percent of the time, in everyone.”
Then come the computer watches, the self-driving vehicles and a generation of young people furious at their elders for living so long and consuming so much of the country’s wealth.

In the novel, a candidate named Matthew Bernstein, the son of a Jewish father and a non-Jewish mother, wins the 2028 election and becomes America’s first Jewish president. Brooks, 79, was watching Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff’s final campaign speech when he thought of Bernstein. Ossoff also has a Jewish father and a non-Jewish mother. Brooks called a close friend.
“God damn it,” he remembers saying. “My entire book is going to come true.”

highlights.title: David Staff obituary
highlights.summary: My former teacher and mentor David Staff, who has died aged 68 of a heart condition, was a cornetto player and period trumpeter, but also well known as a maker of natural trumpets – valveless brass instruments which, in the hands of a good player, produce a distinctive and rich sound.
body: The natural trumpet was the type of trumpet which, for many centuries, accompanied men and horses on the battlefield, but it was also admired by composers such as Bach and Handel, who both wrote music for it.

David got into making his instruments after meeting the natural trumpet maker Frank Tomes in the late 1980s. He learned a lot from Frank, and eventually became his apprentice in 2009, establishing his own workshop at his home near Coddenham in Suffolk. There he would make trumpets from flat sheets of brass: he shaped and soldered his tubes and drew them by hand, and created flared bell sections by hammering and swaging them into shape.

After Frank’s death David took over the business, with valuable input from his friend and fellow instrument maker, Graham Nicholson. Having served as David’s apprentice and hand engraver for 11 years, I will continue the workshop.

highlights.title: Big Tech lost big in the 2026 election
highlights.summary: On Tuesday, millions of American voters went to the polls and voted overwhelmingly for Democrats and against AI. The fight against Big Tech is about to come roaring back, and the fight over data centers is looking even harder for the folks trying to build them.
body: On The Vergecast: blue waves, the confusing business of AI search, and the many thoughts of RAM Altman.

On this episode of The Vergecast, Nilay and David discuss what the 2026 midterms mean for the tech industry going forward. They dig into the self-quarantining echo chamber that is X, the congressional energy likely to be pointed at tech CEOs and AI regulation, and whether anything is actually likely to get done in the next two years.

After that, the hosts turn to AI. Specifically, whether anyone has figured out how to make money on AI. Specifically, whether OpenAI’s explosive growth in web search means much, when even Google can’t figure out how to make money on AI web search. Businesses are scaling back; agents don’t appear to be taking over. There’s a lot of money flowing around the AI world, but is there enough flowing into it to keep everything going? That’s the hard part.
Finally, it’s time for a somewhat abridged Brendan Carr Is a Dummy, the latest on SpaceX’s mobile ambitions, the touchscreen MacBook, RAM Altman, and much more.
points: On Tuesday, millions of American voters went to the polls and voted overwhelmingly for Democrats and against AI.

highlights.title: Global stocks fall amid ‘big worries over AI’ after Democrats’ midterms triumph
highlights.summary: Asian and European markets follow US tech rout with many analysts predicting more waves of selling to come. European and Asian stock markets fell sharply on Friday after the Democrats’ decisive victory in the midterms triggered a rout in US tech stocks a day earlier.
body: A sell-off on Wall Street on Thursday was followed by sharp falls in Asian stock markets on Friday. The investor sentiment then reached London, where the market was, at one stage, poised for its worst day since March.

The FTSE 100 index, which tracks blue-chip shares listed in London, was down as much as 254 points, or 2.35%, at 10,528 points during a wave of selling in morning trading. But by the close of the day it had clawed back some of its losses to be down 1%, helped by a rise in US stocks when Wall Street reopened.
Germany’s Dax index fell by 2%, France’s Cac 40 dropped by 0.8% and Spain’s Ibex lost 0.6%.

Susannah Streeter, the chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, said: “The tech sell-off has intensified, with the pain of the brutal sell-off on Wall Street carried straight through to Asia and knocking sentiment in Europe.

body: In extracts of his autobiography - Sabr - published in the Sydney Morning Herald,, external the former opening batter said Australia had also used the ball-tampering tactic in the Test before the infamous match in Cape Town.
The incident - nicknamed 'sandpapergate' - was widely condemned and led to bans for captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and fellow batter Cameron Bancroft.
"It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us," Khawaja, 39, told the Sydney Morning Herald.

highlights.title: Godzilla Minus Zero Director Takashi Yamazaki Explains the Household Inspiration for the Film’s Big, Brutal Climax
highlights.summary: Warning! Spoilers ahead for Godzilla Minus Zero. Godzilla Minus Zero has the most viscerally violent kaiju battle since Gareth Edwards’ 2014 Godzilla. I’d say it easily surpasses that, even with Godzilla’s atomic-heat-ray-down-the-throat finishing move against the bug-like MUTO in Edwards’ movie…
body: How did writer/director Takashi Yamazaki think about staging this huge, all-out, flesh-ripping, head chopping, arm-tearing kaiju brawl?

“So, I have two cats,” Yamazaki told IGN. “And for the most part, they're very nice and playful with each other, but on a rare occasion I think there's like — I don't know if they're crossing the line between play and actual fighting. I see two creatures fighting each other and I tend to think about my cats when that happens.”

Incredible. Anyone with multiple cats knows exactly what Yamazaki is talking about, and the inspiration is hard to unsee. Ghidorah, even from his first scene of destruction, comes off as somewhat cat-like as he peeks at fleeing people in between buildings, like a cat hunting, before razing the city with his terrifying zaps of thunder breath. Then when he’s done, he goes and curls up to take a long nap in a kaiju-sized bed, also known as a mountain crater.

highlights.title: Justin Timberlake Teases New Music: “I’ve Been Chef-ing”
highlights.summary: The Grammy- and Emmy-winning singer hints at fresh material he's worked on with Don Toliver, Quavo, Pharrell and Timbaland and explains why he was originally told hit "SexyBack" wasn't "gonna work."
body: It’s been a little over a year since Justin Timberlake wrapped his Forget Tomorrow world tour, promoting his sixth solo album Everything I Thought It Was, released in 2024, but he’s already cooking up something new.
The Grammy- and Emmy-winning singer said he’s “been working” in Miami and hinted at new music, particularly in the form of collaborations with Pharrell Williams, Quavo, Don Toliver and Timbaland.

In the video, where Timberlake revisited some of his most beloved songs, he spoke at length specifically about working with Toliver, explaining how his son played a role in his “easy decision” to clear a “Rock Your Body” sample for Toliver’s “Body.”

“As soon as I heard it, I was like, yeah, of course,” Timberlake said. “My 11-year-old, Silas, Don Toliver, that’s his guy, I remember asking him… and he was like, ‘You gotta do it.’ So that was an easy yes. I also really love that whole album.”
